details: Twice in one run, two shapes, one rule (principle 6): the quiet check runs changed tests with another runner and a narrower set than the gate.
failing_case: `relay precheck` on f8b4fee or 4ba4199 is green; the gate on them is red.
pass_cases: relay precheck runs the test files changed on the branch under plain python3 (the gate's runner) and RuleTestsComplete, and is red on both shas with the gate's message.
A branch that changes no test file adds under 5 s to precheck.
A changed test that passes keeps precheck green; one too slow for STEP_TIMEOUT is a red line, not a skip.
reason: tests/test_precheck.py TestChangedTests::test_a_changed_test_importing_a_module_the_gate_lacks_is_red passes at head and fails at 54bb779e.
findings.summary: Precheck misses tests the gate runs differently

details: CONFIRMED by running it. STEP_TIMEOUT (60 s) was sized for "about 10 s for the whole precheck when healthy"; the new step
runs whole library test files in one process under that same budget. Measured under the gate's runner on this machine
(other lanes running): test_gate 109.8 s, test_setup 37.4 s, test_setup_off 38.8 s, test_precheck 26.6 s. On master in the
last week 29 commits touched tests/test_gate.py and 11 touched tests/test_setup.py; a lane on lib/relay_gate.py is being built
now (wt/gate-rerun) and will very likely change test_gate.py. HIGH: fails on ordinary use, and the false "the gate would be
red" sends a worker to fix what is not broken. The item's own pass case ("too slow for STEP_TIMEOUT is a red line") is met in
letter, but the item assumes changed tests fit the budget; the fix inside the design is a budget of this step's own.
evidence: FAIL changed tests took longer than 60 s
precheck: RED (the gate would be red; fix these first)
$ python3 -W ignore::ResourceWarning tests/run_unittest.py tests.test_gate  -> Ran 23 tests in 109.414s OK
$ ... tests.test_setup -> Ran 46 tests in 36.754s OK;  tests.test_setup_off -> Ran 33 tests in 38.287s OK
$ git log --since=2026-10-21 --format=%h master -- tests/test_gate.py | wc -l -> 29;  -- tests/test_setup.py -> 11
failing_case: A copy of HEAD 1e186223 with one comment line appended to tests/test_gate.py (all tests green): relay_precheck.run prints
"RED  changed tests / FAIL changed tests took longer than 60 s / precheck: RED (the gate would be red; fix these first)"
after 70 s. The gate would be green. Because the quiet check is `relay precheck -C <wt> && (<check>)` (cycle.js:114), the
worker's, fixer's and checker's check never runs on such a branch, every loop. Same on 4ba4199 (test_setup + test_setup_off).
Should be: green (or red only with a real test failure) for a branch whose changed tests pass under the gate's runner.
fix_hint: Give the step its own budget (for example a CHANGED_TESTS_TIMEOUT of 230 s, under the 4-minute command limit, set as the
step's deadline in run() through a per-step table), and say that budget in the timeout line. Optionally split the changed
modules across a few processes (parallel_unittest already does that for the gate) to keep the loop short.
pass_cases: 1. A branch whose only change is a comment in tests/test_gate.py (passes alone under python3 tests/run_unittest.py in about 110 s): check_changed_tests returns [] and run() prints "ok   changed tests".
2. A branch changing tests/test_setup.py and tests/test_setup_off.py, both green (about 76 s together): "ok   changed tests".

3. A changed test that sleeps longer than this step's own budget: still "RED  changed tests" with "took longer than <n> s" naming the budget actually used (the item's pass case: a red line, not a skip).
4. A branch with no changed test: the step still runs only the registry test and adds under 5 s.
5. The other three steps keep their 60 s budget (a slow bin/types-lint is still red at 60 s).
reason: test_a_changed_test_slower_than_the_other_steps_budget_is_green and test_the_other_steps_keep_their_own_budget pass; the first fails at 1e186223.
findings.summary: a green branch that touches a slow test file (test_gate.py 110 s, test_setup + test_setup_off 76 s) is RED on every precheck, so the quiet check never reaches the worker's own check

details: CONFIRMED by running it at 4ba4199. names = changed modules + RULES_REGISTRY_TEST go to one subprocess.run; a timeout kills the
process and keeps no output, so the 0.6 s registry verdict is lost whenever the changed tests are slow. F1's larger budget
makes this rarer but not impossible. The temp-repo test test_the_registry_test_runs_and_its_message_shows uses a fast changed
test, so it does not cover this shape. Size: 10 min.
evidence: FAIL changed tests took longer than 60 s
fixer report: "Not run: precheck on f8b4fee / 4ba4199 themselves (covered by temp-repo tests of both shapes)."
failing_case: Detached worktree at 4ba4199 (the item's second failing case; changed tests: tests.test_setup, tests.test_setup_off).
relay_precheck.run prints "RED  changed tests / FAIL changed tests took longer than 60 s"; no RuleTestsComplete line and no
name of the unlisted class. The item's pass case asks for red "with the gate's message" (missing
tests.test_setup.Setup in RuleTestsComplete). The fixer did not run precheck on either sha ("Not run" in its report).
fix_hint: Run RULES_REGISTRY_TEST in its own python3 tests/run_unittest.py call first (0.6 s) and keep its failing tail; then run the
pass_cases: 1. 4ba4199: precheck output contains "RuleTestsComplete" and "tests.test_setup.Setup" (the registry's own assertion message), whatever the changed tests' time.
2. Temp repo: a changed test that sleeps past the budget and a red registry stand-in: output has both the registry failure and the timeout line.
3. f8b4fee: output still contains "No module named 'pytest'".
4. A branch with no changed test and a green registry: "ok   changed tests".
findings.summary: the registry test runs in the same process as the changed tests, so a slow changed test hides its message: on 4ba4199 precheck says only 'took longer than 60 s', not the gate's RuleTestsComplete failure
